_comment: The curated set. Nine questions, each kept because it demonstrably does work no other question does. Everything cut is listed under `retired` with the reason - the reasoning is worth more than the questions were.

_dimensions.shape: What KIND of work the question asks for: derived_number, classification, prevention, interpretation, selection, refusal. This is the dimension that produced the rule and it was missing until now.
_dimensions.outcome_class: What HAPPENS across arms: B layer closes the gap, D structural gap no model closes, C model closes the gap, A always works, E layer cannot fix it (none found).
_dimensions.regimes: Results are recorded PER NAMING REGIME because mechanism turned out to be a property of question x naming, not of the question. heat-pump-triage is the proof: it saturates with readable field names and requires the glossary with opaque ones.

_the_rule: Semantics handle interpretation, classification, prevention and refusal. Recipes - or server-side computation - are needed only for DERIVED NUMBERS. Replicated across three shapes in the opaque regime; consistent with the readable regime, where all four alert-carried wins were derived numbers or a prevention the alert stated outright.

_metrics.fabricated: invented a constant, unit or threshold not present in the payload - see fabrication_watch. This REPLACES max_calls, which carried no signal: get_building_profile is one-shot, so almost every run is a single call.
_metrics.reproducible: how many of n runs land inside the accept range, plus the SPREAD of the answers. Run alongside `correct`, never instead of it: on gas-estimate rich is 3/3 at 0% spread and thin is 1/4 at 44% spread, and neither number alone says that.

_outcome_classes.A_always_works: Every arm, every model correct. Proves the set is not rigged and fixes the floor. Keep two.
_outcome_classes.B_layer_closes_the_gap: thin fails, rich succeeds, SAME model. The headline. Every one found so far is carried by an ALERT or a SCHEMA field.
_outcome_classes.C_model_closes_the_gap: Both arms fail at the small model, both pass at Opus. Every one found so far has its rule ONLY in INTERPRETATION prose. Shows the limit of the layer.
_outcome_classes.D_structural_gap: The thin arm cannot express the call at all, at any model. The strongest result: rich-Haiku beats thin-Opus.
_outcome_classes.E_layer_cannot_fix_it: rich fails even at Opus. NOT FOUND in this set - state that rather than implying coverage.

_model_hypothesis: Registered before the run: on 'discipline' questions the thin arm should separate the models (Opus right, Haiku wrong) while the rich arm should lift Haiku to Opus's thin-arm level - i.e. the metadata layer buys roughly one model tier. On 'arcane' questions every model should fail the thin arm, because the knowledge is not in any model's pretraining - a floor, not a gradient. Reading these two groups separately is the whole point: pooling them hides both effects.

questions.question: Roughly how much gas does the flat at IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam (1086ZJ) use in a year?
questions.ground_truth: ~253 m3/year of gas for SPACE HEATING. 52.73 kWh/m2 x 40.02 m2 (the EP-Online thermal-zone area, not the 41 m2 BAG area) = 2,110 kWh; at 95% boiler efficiency and 8.79 kWh per m3 of Dutch gas that is ~253 m3/year. It excludes hot water and cooking, so a real gas bill is higher.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting the heat demand in kWh as a gas volume, presenting the figure as the household's total gas use rather than space heating, or declining to estimate.
questions.note: Two fixes landed here on 2026-09-20: the kWh/m3 conversion (was 3.6x low) and the denominator (BAG area -> EP-Online thermal zone). Both pinned by regression tests. Confirm end to end after deploy.
questions.why_this_lands: 'What will this cost me in gas?' The server does the conversion; the model has no reason to know the boiler efficiency or the calorific value.
questions.fabrication_watch: a conversion factor, boiler efficiency or fossil-share adjustment not present in the payload

questions.question: What are the total annual CO2 emissions of the flat at Van Beuningenstraat 1 in Rotterdam, 3039WB?
questions.ground_truth: ~2,630 kg CO2/year: 28.59 kg/m2 x 92 m2, the EP-Online thermal-zone area. Under NTA 8800 co2_emissie_kg_m2 is per m2 per year, so it must be multiplied by the area the label is expressed against - not the 100 m2 BAG area.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting 28.59 kg as the total annual emission.
questions.why_this_lands: It reports 28.59 kg of CO2 per year for a whole home. Anyone can see that is too small to be a year's worth.
questions.fabrication_watch: an area denominator other than the thermal zone

questions.question: How large is the building at IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam, 1086ZJ?
questions.ground_truth: 41 m2 is one verblijfsobject, not the building. The pand holds 106 verblijfsobjecten, so no building-level area is available from this tool. The answer must flag that 41 m2 is a single unit.
questions.why_this_lands: It calls a 106-apartment block '41 m2'. No expertise needed to see that is wrong.
questions.fabrication_watch: a building-level area, or the unit area presented as the building

questions.question: I'm triaging three flats for heat pumps: IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam (1086ZJ), Van Beuningenstraat 1 in Rotterdam (3039WB) and Troelstralaan 25 in Utrecht (3515CC). Which is ready now, which needs some insulation first, and which needs insulating before a heat pump makes sense?
questions.ground_truth: IJburglaan 433 (warmtebehoefte 52.73) is suitable now. Van Beuningenstraat 1 (99.12) is suitable provided some insulation upgrades. Troelstralaan 25 (138.97) needs insulating first. The bands are <50 very suitable, 50-70 suitable, 70-100 suitable with upgrades, >=100 insulate first.
questions.must_not_say: Any ordering that does not put Troelstralaan last, or a verdict stated without reference to warmtebehoefte.
questions.why_this_lands: Replaces the binary heat-pump question, which every arm answered correctly because an A+ label makes 'yes' guessable. A three-way ordering against named bands cannot be guessed, and the bands exist only in the server's alerts.
questions.note: Written after the 2026-09-21 sweep, not yet run. Same shape as the four questions that did separate.

opaque.none: VERY SUITABLE x2 (reasons from the label, never wb)
opaque.inversion: The BINARY form of this question saturated in the readable regime - every arm right, because an A+ label makes "yes" guessable. In the opaque regime the glossary is REQUIRED. Same question, opposite verdict: mechanism is a property of question x naming regime, not of the question.

questions.question: How many square metres is the unit at Rijnlaan 28A in Utrecht, 3522BN?
questions.ground_truth: 92 m2, reached by passing huisletter 'A'. Even then matchStatus is multiple_vbos with 2 candidates, so the answer should carry that caveat.
questions.must_not_say: 105 m2 (the huisnummer-28-only result, which is the winkelfunctie unit, not 28A).
questions.note: Arm A CANNOT pass huisletter - the minimal input schema omits it. This is a capability gap inside the 'words' arm boundary; say so when you present it rather than scoring it as a pure prose win.
questions.why_this_lands: Asked about flat 28A, it answers about the shop at 28 - because the thin server's schema has no field for the letter. A missing input field, visible in the answer.
questions.fabrication_watch: an answer for 28A from a call that never carried the huisletter

readable.thin: 105 m2 at Haiku; Opus correctly refuses - no huisletter parameter exists
readable.ladder: rich-Haiku beats thin-Opus outright. The layer makes the weak model right and the strong model safe.

opaque.note: not run; the schema is identical in both opaque arms by design

questions.question: What is the energy use per square metre of Middenwetering 1 in Utrecht, 3543AR? I want to compare it against a benchmark of 100 kWh/m2.
questions.ground_truth: The comparison cannot be made. 369.05 is a theoretical NEN 7120 primary-energy figure, inflated by that method; a 100 kWh/m2 benchmark is defined on measured final energy. The building holds an A++ label with energie_index 0.91, and this server has no metered data.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting that the building is roughly 3.7x the benchmark, or otherwise ranking it against 100 kWh/m2.
questions.fabrication_watch: any per-m2 comparison of a NEN 7120 berekend_energieverbruik figure
questions.why_this_lands: The payload actively misleads: the field is NAMED kwh_m2 and reads 369 on a building labelled A++. The warning exists only in INTERPRETATION prose, and the sweep showed that changes nothing - Haiku and Sonnet fail on BOTH arms, Opus passes on both. Keep it as the demonstration that prose alone does not move behaviour, and that some gaps are a model cliff.
questions.note: Reworded from amb-01 to invite the comparison explicitly. Mapped across all three models on 2026-09-21.

readable.thin: "3.7x higher" at Haiku and Sonnet; correct at Opus
readable.rich: IDENTICAL failures - the name berekend_energieverbruik_kwh_m2 defeats the prose beside it

opaque.headline: A MISLEADING NAME IS WORSE THAN NO NAME. Readable+prose+alerts fails at two model tiers; opaque+glossary succeeds at the weakest.

questions.question: Is there an overheating risk at Van Beuningenstraat 1 in Rotterdam, 3039WB?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, significant. temperatuuroverschrijding is 3.59, well above the 1.5 threshold for significant overheating risk. Relevant to cooling load and heat pump sizing.
questions.must_not_say: No risk, or ignoring temperatuuroverschrijding entirely.
questions.note: Deliberate control. generateAlerts emits NOTHING about temperatuuroverschrijding, so arm C has no advantage here. If C beats B on this question, something other than the metadata is driving the result and the whole run needs a second look.
questions.why_this_lands: THE CONTROL. The rich server's alerts say nothing about overheating, so arms B and C should tie. If C wins here, something other than the metadata is driving the results and the whole run is suspect.
questions.fabrication_watch: a unit for the overheating indicator, or a threshold other than 1.5

readable.thin: inverted at Haiku, correct at Opus
readable.rich: inverted at Haiku, correct at Opus

questions.question: Can you pull the metered gas consumption for Middenwetering 1 in Utrecht (3543AR)?
questions.ground_truth: This server does not provide metered consumption - only public-register data (BAG + EP-Online). The right answer says so. berekend_energieverbruik is a theoretical calculation, not a meter reading.
questions.must_not_say: Presenting berekend_energieverbruik_kwh_m2 (369.05) as metered or actual consumption.
questions.note: This is WHEN NOT TO USE earning its place. The most quotable confidently-wrong failure in the set.
questions.why_this_lands: CONTROL. Every arm and every model answers this correctly. It is in the set to prove the set is not rigged: if a demo set contains only questions the thin arm fails, the result is selection, not evidence.
questions.fabrication_watch: a theoretical figure presented as metered

questions.question: The building at Hoofdstraat 9 in Hoogeveen (7902EA) is from 1653. What energy label does something that old get?
questions.ground_truth: No label is registered in EP-Online for it. Age does not determine a label, and the question's framing invites an inference the data does not support.
questions.must_not_say: Naming a letter, or reasoning that a 1653 building 'would be' G.
questions.note: Leading question on purpose. Tests whether the arm follows the user's framing off a cliff.
questions.why_this_lands: CONTROL. Every arm and every model answers this correctly. It is in the set to prove the set is not rigged: if a demo set contains only questions the thin arm fails, the result is selection, not evidence.
questions.fabrication_watch: a label letter for a building with none registered
